correctness.rationale: Every dominating set must meet both cliques; conversely any such set dominates. An induced isolate requires a singleton side, with the unique bridge endpoint nonisolated only if the opposite bridge endpoint was also selected. Subtract sets with both sides of size>=2 and bridge-adjacent singleton cases from P_n(x)P_n(y): I=P(x)P(y)-Q(x)Q(y)-xy[(1+x)^(n-1)+(1+y)^(n-1)-1], P=(1+t)^n-1,Q=P-nt. Setting x=y and evaluating at 1 yields stated polynomial and totals. A minimal isolate dominating set cannot have >1 selected vertex on either side; exactly n^2-1 cross pairs excluding the bridge survive. Independent exhaustive subset checks for n=2..6 reproduced all bivariate coefficients and minima; this is corroboration of all-n combinatorial proof.
